strings.07c6d57177d09a4f0641e65037cb8709e1b94cbf: Start tonight's checks with what you use.
strings.f5d1b9e9330df6b95ed8736d00a804a274662327: We reviewed account protection, malicious packages, application authentication and permissions, and updates on services in Japan. The 37 topics are organized to help you find necessary measures and primary sources.
strings.a566886a2e1514e399234f540833da76272e0683: The 6th report at 21 advises checking linked services such as email and Google, as well as browser sync, in addition to disconnecting all sessions. Proceed from another trusted device.
strings.e8f3d19734362a2e47d980e562f3267e15496a5e: For those managing development and build environments
strings.4a4eb0d61b3d5c6088de9d0326e6b732ccbb7e91: Check the affected npm and PyPI packages and versions. If malicious versions have run, review environment isolation, revocation of keys they could access, and whether rebuilding is necessary.
strings.d8d3f5af9197bfe4d072bba9004ec61a80566d81: For administrators of applications and public-facing services
strings.51fe405af3e08cf7e6e96bde0bfedc54a79d4b27: Review Japanese PHP/Brotli alerts and the conditions affecting Frappe, MISP, SAML, NocoDB, and others. Camel may require configuration even after updating.
strings.dd5909db87f7c2c34c6ffe006b421f7e3c34baf9: For users of delivery and booking services
strings.0f442b7bd87f8eba6321788aeceabe130d578b2f: Blastmail's notice covers 345 contracts, and the resumption time remains undetermined. Even if someone knows your hotel booking details, verify payment links through official support channels.
strings.0843ae83803c20412f3f2e832e7a135dc23f5b17: Frappe Builder: SSRF in image retrieval and permissions for AI use
strings.346a29900a553f590b6f4789c3d6ef1988eb4efe: The developer published 3 advisories at 14:58 JST. They cover authenticated users controlling image retrieval destinations, reaching internal destinations through redirects and DNS re-resolution, and insufficient authorization for improve_prompt, which uses an AI provider key. They do not describe compromise of every server by any unauthenticated user.
strings.f3be593c8e18ef80ad6dcd127d00511d2f18ef2f: Check the requirements for Builder 1.36.1 or later and Frappe v16.36.1 or later. Review image retrieval destinations, publicly stored content, and AI usage logs. If updating is not possible, consider restricting the affected APIs and temporarily removing AI keys.
strings.ab646bdaa4d8942a23d244a9bdd2435822bce7dd: 4 additional NocoDB issues: authentication processing and the role of rate limits
strings.f441e44604c694622f6bab2acc26639f0564fbd9: CVE-2026-116120–116123 are CNA records concerning resource consumption during signup and reset, signup races, differences in sign-in information, and limits on authentication attempts. The official PublicApiLimiterGuard explicitly states a design that relies on a reverse proxy or similar component for rate limiting, and the current signup processing also includes withSignupClaim. An increase in record identifiers alone does not establish that every version remains unfixed.
strings.ce4a02f9ab423383978e6eeccd74451347f007cd: Check rate limits for externally exposed signup, reset, and login endpoints, including proxy-side controls. Compare unusual signup and session revocation logs with the version in use, and treat the earliest shipped fixed version as undetermined.
strings.52e72c623bacae5ab452115ebe9eca46651bcd8f: GitHub malware advisories describe mining programs and persistence mechanisms run through postinstall in dsh-plugin-blender-3d 0.2.1 and @walknpm/todo-cli 2.0.1. Behavior differs depending on whether root access or passwordless sudo is available. This does not mean that all npm packages or Blender itself have been compromised.
strings.9480c380e4ae8d26835633ace041b020ff2f3298: Check installation records for the affected versions. If they have run, isolate the environment, investigate persistence, external communications, and access to credentials, and revoke any necessary keys from a safe environment.
strings.39f7a3fc40569c6f9b97449bbf27e782c75ad88d: Hotel Tavinos: beware of payment links even from someone who knows your booking
strings.9411969fc6f61812f366b4b787e52eb10b05dcbd: Suspicious messages affected some bookings at the 3 Hamamatsucho, Asakusa, and Kyoto properties that met both conditions: made by 9/21 and with a stay date on or after 9/21. The notice explains that booking information may have been viewed and obtained through TEMAIRAZU. It does not confirm disclosure of all bookings or a new intrusion at this time.
strings.560baae65422d91f366a4bce2fe1656928af4f04: Even if a message contains accurate booking details, do not enter information or transfer money through its URL; verify through the property's or booking site's official support channel. If you have already entered card information, contact your card issuer.
strings.ec25f0f79283f2ab140ae1eced3d5b9c04a49e01: libgsf: boundary checks in OLE2 file parsing
strings.1a293f14bcf2ad33a30f07ccadd10943a6d8f292: CVE-2026-116124 is a CNA entry concerning the OLE2 parser through version 1.14.60. A 9/26 commit fixing an out-of-bounds write was confirmed in GNOME's official mirror. The original GitLab page returned a challenge screen despite HTTP success, so its body could not be read. This is not a newly issued fix, and the earliest distributed fixed version remains undetermined.
strings.3c1335e2d126dc180b987175f3bdaf68e77f411e: Inventory libgsf bundled with document parsing and conversion processes, and check which distributions include the fix. Restrict the environments and privileges used to process untrusted OLE2 documents.
strings.f022e4de16e40f548e5c8832dac20bde8ec68d14: agent-teams-ai: boundaries of the local HTTP service
strings.1bc58078982c2be86aa26d7fe5e1f50242b48ad7: CVE-2026-116228 is a CNA entry concerning insufficient authentication in the Local HTTP Service through version 2.17.10. Official code confirmed default handling of localhost origins, CORS conditions that broaden depending on configuration, and listening on the specified host. Unconditional compromise from an external webpage under every configuration has not been verified.
strings.15e677a9914987d32139d390d4f133faa77d782c: Check the local HTTP service's listening address, CORS_ORIGIN, execution user, and local users' privileges. The earliest fixed version remains undetermined.
strings.9e341d9bc45da36502ad888b828e7fe67b8e93c6: JPCERT/CC: PHP update and Japanese Brotli alert
strings.a6f5d4e3abae5e1d071c2460dae97410fe24e190: At 16:25 JST, JPCERT/CC added information on PHP demonstrations, environment-dependent conditions, and upload progress mitigation, and published a Brotli alert. JVN also listed Brotli at 18:00. These are updates to guidance for Japan, not separate new PHP/Brotli CVEs.
strings.eecbefc20046657173c701a2d02f86afb47083f0: For PHP, continue updating to fixed versions and investigating compromise, and check session.upload_progress.enabled=0 for CVE-2026-115560 and restart all workers. For Brotli, check branch-specific fixes in 1.0.10 / 1.1.1 / 1.2.1 and guidance for products that bundle it.
strings.8eaffd6df3db24bb1f765bc0c4a592528955d95e: @worca/app: malware advisory for affected RC versions
strings.062d078d5ba753c4a32cafbe89b7a66bf6a6bc06: GitHub classifies @worca/app 1.14.0-rc.2 / 1.14.0-rc.4 as malware and advises treating devices on which it was run or installed as compromised. The public record does not specify the number of affected organizations or when the intrusion began.
strings.dca0ec999ff54821b5e4452684b9e9ede7fc7fa5: Isolate and investigate environments where the affected versions were installed. Rotate keys and secrets from another safe device, and do not consider recovery complete simply because the package has been removed.
strings.7ee21f47ab498141aae84f3583e26bdc11550ba7: Blastmail: total rises to 345 contracts; resumption time remains undetermined
strings.16f2decb10999fbe666c67ad5c8484e523e1b6b8: An external investigation newly confirmed exposure of information other than subscriber information for 1 additional contract. The operator states that the total is 345 contracts and that individual notifications to all 345 have been completed. This does not mean exposure involving 345 people or all recipients. The management interface, API, and delivery remain suspended; the next report is scheduled for around 10/27 12:00.
strings.a1d7b1c593fe8d094853483fa6f080edfff03437: Compare the information affected under each contract with the latest notification, and continue alternative delivery arrangements, inquiry handling, and vigilance against fraudulent emails. Do not treat completion of notifications as the end of the investigation or authorization to resume.
strings.4ffde87d12f7161c83f4506b2d6e7a13c2093150: Game and desktop utilities: handling external input
strings.02f724d65a464989ffdbbe8b1cc8a668be1ee59a: FFXIV Teamcraft CVE-2026-116229 concerns clipboard IPC in the renderer; Plague Inc Evolved CVE-2026-116230 concerns deserialization of Workshop scenarios. Teamcraft 11.4.32 was published on 10/13 and is not a new fix issued tonight. Avoid generalizing these issues to every part of the games or to ordinary browsing alone.
strings.773c09922ae4001894d89e02c5257d812c6ea93d: Compare fix guidance for Teamcraft 11.4.32, Plague Inc Evolved 1.24.0.4, and other applicable versions with your environment, and restrict untrusted scenarios and renderer input.
strings.b892c94519281bb57349405e8e994bc7f47e2418: Oray X5 Pro: newline and file handling through configuration values
strings.9f586dd5d664153da6d6acb077e2def0296596c8: CVE-2026-116231–116237 are CNA entries concerning configuration processing for Ser2net, SNMP, Dnsmasq, IPsec, L2TP, PPPoE, and other components in Pugongying X5 Pro 7.6.1. Newline injection and uploads should not collectively be generalized as unauthenticated external intrusion; access to administrative operations and privilege requirements need further confirmation.
strings.d22e27213580ca326c4c313d245a36afba3a5c9b: Check the model, firmware, management interface exposure, and configuration change history. The earliest fixed version remains undetermined, so review vendor guidance and restrictions on unnecessary administrative access.
strings.3026e4f72957b347217c757b18b037b363035c92: MISP Guard: check sharing policy evaluation
strings.29a13ed0341f4ca9eb8d85823ed0586d73213413: CVE-2026-116372 allows distribution filters to be bypassed through successful responses other than 200; 116469 allows bypasses through letter casing in tags, categories, and sharing group UUIDs. The developer addressed these in commits at 16:53 / 18:25 JST. This does not confirm compromise of all of MISP itself or disclosure of all feed data.
strings.a7bd365a4bec2823796c745247c4dad0398c30b0: Check that the running code includes both fixes, and review permission settings such as TLP and distribution history. The earliest distributed release containing the fixes has not been established in this review.
strings.700f8963526b3b8e608ee18825f3412e0084c8f3: npm publish-poc packages: publishing permissions in the installation environment
strings.0e03a4a05c6ec97bbf3ca58d867c537917a91a3c: The 7 affected versions of publish-poc-test3 reportedly attempt to publish using the environment's npm credentials during postinstall. publish-poc-base 1.0.7 prepares a temporary file containing a README fragment and credentials, but the description states that this version deletes it before publishing or communicating externally. Do not count both as successful external transmission.
strings.a23f1ddbf5ad1ca23f98b819ac270a3b116159eb: Check the affected versions, CI installation logs, and npm publishing history. If suspicious publications are found, revoke the relevant tokens and review dependencies and publishing permissions.
strings.24786fc32636464134fde40d889e4612d69b1608: 2 PyPI cases: transmission of basic device information and analysis classifications
strings.d3a2e5332db339e4f60c9c4980f550e9b68f09a6: zagents-framework 6.25.30.10b5 / 99.25.30.10b5 and changes-lxc-wrapper 0.0.0 / 0.1.0 are recorded as sending basic device information during installation or import. GitHub categorizes them as malware, while the original analysis classifies them as PROBABLY_PENTEST. Do not equate them with large-scale credential theft incidents.
strings.14f1a6e8bc9ab1639b86f479e96a414168e993a8: Check their intended use and how they were installed, and exclude unnecessary affected packages. If they have run, investigate the destinations and actual impact.
strings.304ec63ca27f01f02760022b4ccbc3292452f2a3: BRAIN2: service credentials left in installation logs
strings.a5945014c01702ccbeed94dfaabe1f7039b1664e: CVE-2026-112250 concerns plaintext passwords left in setup logs in BRAIN2 3.09 and earlier when SQL Server Integrated Security is combined with a specified Windows service account. The logs are usually in the installing administrator's temporary directory; the description does not say they are unconditionally exposed to standard users.
strings.936005e47547f87508a140a97f8d477d4c140836: Update to 3.10 or later, and check secure removal and access permissions for the relevant setup logs. Change credentials for service accounts suspected of exposure.
strings.5f484279443f06b2fd718c065c277bd76576da82: CVE-2026-89209 is an authentication bypass under conditions involving reuse of a valid SAML response in IdP-initiated SSO. It affects module versions below 3.6.29 for Mendix 9 and below 4.2.4 for 10/11. It does not state that merely creating an arbitrary SAML response is sufficient.
strings.72c1faa6b960fa41f098c2419efb4a7d1438f5b5: Update the SAML module in use to 3.6.29 or 4.2.4 or later. If an immediate update is not possible, consult the developer's guidance on disabling IdP-initiated SSO.
strings.039a38e6f3ffb2f8af8250282f80cb090f6acfa2: Additional WordPress issues: check privileges and individual fixed versions
strings.087d421aed0af3662a92313da3e2be9f121816cb: The original sources confirm privilege requirements of Contributor for SQL injection in JetEngine 3.9.0 and earlier, Author for SQL injection in Media Library Assistant 3.42 and earlier, and Contributor for insufficient authorization in AI Engine 3.8.6 and earlier. These and the other XSS and CSRF entries are not all treated as unauthenticated RCE or confirmed exploitation.
strings.0cd070c998e3fa3b8424dc0310e589af277284d2: Check for JetEngine 3.9.0.1, Media Library Assistant 3.43, and AI Engine 3.8.7 or later, and review contributor privileges and installed plugins. For the remaining individual records, use the NVD index to check product-specific fixes.
strings.fcf289b58d6bd7cdb6006439bc9ce68db8b505d6: libimobiledevice: protocol responses from connected peers
strings.c23942cd27ee927855732d75dea1773c369ccf0a: CVE-2026-116258–116262 are CNA entries concerning memory handling in AFC, Web Inspector, and other components through version 1.4.0. The device info entries also include issues with local conditions. Official code was checked, but details could not be retrieved from the researcher's dynamically rendered site, so the full connection and pairing requirements and earliest fixed version remain undetermined.
strings.fa87e8e4e65cf85fb186c601c526f223d897f8c4: Check device management tools, bundled versions, and the devices trusted for connection. Do not interpret this as all iPhones being vulnerable to compromise merely by browsing any website; isolate processing of suspicious devices and protocol responses.
strings.aad8fbb26c5d876e2d362c83d0a4899ff45ec749: GMO: check linked services and browser sync as well as all sessions
strings.cddbe5974db9b206a1edd210dfb51bc7a5365007: The guidance advises signing out all devices and all sessions from another safe device, changing passwords for FX, securities, email, Google, and other services, and using MFA. It also adds removal of unfamiliar linked apps, forwarding settings, extensions, and registered devices, and keeping browser sync off until checks are complete. This does not confirm infection of every connected device.
strings.38d36deaceb476e66fe8ea72bef9b24e42511645: Check guidance through official support channels, revoke all sessions, and review newly added authentication methods and integrations. Run a full scan and keep a disconnected backup; for optional PC investigations, check the scope of the prior confirmation document.
strings.b3ef0ef6d47aafbb4a482b04277f9a825cbdb49c: Qt: denial of service caused by a malicious HTTP/2 peer
strings.1dcab59202c2c940a625abe8b4e22a4976b3d7ce: CVE-2026-96432 concerns QNetworkAccessManager stopping while processing a sequence of responses from a malicious or compromised HTTP/2 server. The official table lists affected versions as 6.8.0–6.8.9 and 6.9.0–6.11.2. It does not confirm code execution through applications using Qt or compromise of all Qt products.
strings.495e27e1fd5bfdfbe915cb11f959434937df6c45: Check the applicable release branches, such as Qt 6.8.10 / 6.11.3, and update applications and bundled libraries. Also review control over connection destinations and restart monitoring.
strings.ba9d927bca9e3b092407b4d84861e1446b29247e: Image uploads: temporary files and deletion permissions
strings.bf0244c393b75a39c777ff157ef682e47f5e7c8f: PictShare CVE-2026-116263 involves a race caused by predictable temporary filenames that allows content to be replaced after inspection. A fix dated 10/18 and the v3.7.2 tag were confirmed, but the GitHub Release API returned 404. EasyImage CVE-2026-116223 concerns deletion permissions, with a related hardening commit confirmed on 10/24. The conditions differ between the two products.
strings.8ac71afb5f852d670e262a4974ee122a41941164: For PictShare, check the tag corresponding to 3.7.2 and inclusion of the fix; for EasyImage, check the relevant fix and authentication and storage destination settings. Do not infer an arbitrary version number as a new earliest fixed version.
strings.bb50866b3672c7ed004009f4cb42222e4f7c600a: Logsign SIEM / Liman MYS: product-specific administrative paths
strings.ca2f0f6c0d5d59be2e515e053fd3bd48dae90a76: The CNA records path traversal in Logsign SIEM from 6.4.120 up to but excluding 6.4.122, and password recovery in Liman MYS from 2.3.4-1124 up to but excluding 2.3.5-1131, as separate issues. The national authority's original notification pages were dynamically rendered and their bodies could not be retrieved, so exploit conditions and actual exploitation were not independently confirmed in this review.
strings.2f1b6f256752d57bf11530ad0051c2c2f38c5416: Compare distributor guidance for Logsign 6.4.122, Liman 2.3.5-1131, and other applicable versions with the release branch in use, and review exposure of administrative paths, recovery procedures, and related logs.
strings.5fe72b53019648dfa8116bdee44a097bf903f931: PyPI netweavex: fetching remote code on import
strings.e8b72832647891963b559617bf2aa5ca2e795c90: The affected versions are netweavex 1.1.0 / 1.1.1 / 1.1.2. The original analysis describes copying a legitimate package, obfuscation, and fetching and executing code from GitHub on import. It also states that the retrieval destination was a placeholder at the time of analysis, and does not confirm successful theft of any specific information.
strings.f560cbcf1bfaf148c963856ccfcf793f0571fb5d: Check installation records without running the affected versions. If they have run, investigate external communications and execution history, and revoke secrets and rebuild as appropriate to the exposure.
strings.5d0b3b7e03aefae62c03389deca1be08601220a4: The developer advisory for CVE-2026-96581 was published at 14:32 JST, before the previous cutoff. It describes conditions under attribute multitenancy in which a create action with upsert that accepts primary keys or similar values can update or retrieve another tenant's records. Not every create action or Ash application has this configuration.
strings.a179262285dc700c30b52ad1c8a35bbbaffa962e: Check for Ash 3.37.2 or later, and review cross-tenant upserts and record movement history. Also note the exception that the temporary upsert_condition workaround does not work with Mnesia.
strings.993fc7f57cf6c3003951d5118ea95b91946945c8: Apache Camel: Docling configuration is still needed after updating
strings.ab3d96168eee871c9da847e5363a48779f14dc5e: 5 advisories published on 10/22 have been supplemented to reflect their inclusion in NVD. Docling input and output paths, expiration of Keycloak introspection results, expression evaluation in AWS2-S3 object names, and information disclosure in CoAP errors involve distinct conditions. The Keycloak issue applies when token introspection is enabled, which is not the default.
strings.48fe272a475fd4a17d46de6c46cd45caa44fe6ba: Update to versions such as 4.18.5 / 4.22.2 / 4.23.0, as applicable. Where external input can specify a Docling output destination, configure outputBaseDirectory even after updating. Check handling of S3 headers and expired tokens.
strings.0993f12da2e2f0e7383185c081d9948958ee2ddf: SOEM: device responses on the same EtherCAT network
strings.cd0134febfffe0e0125a3f9b2cd383fe72a2f83e: RT-Labs documentation dated 9/21 describes 6 issues affecting SOEM 2.0.0 and earlier. They require a malicious or compromised EtherCAT device to return invalid responses to the master. Insufficient validation of lengths, cumulative quantities, array indices, and similar values may cause memory corruption, information disclosure, or shutdown. General internet reachability alone is not sufficient.
strings.3a900b138eeca1932f96a5347108edb08963ed4e: Check with the product vendor whether SOEM 2.0.1 or later is integrated. Review device additions to the EtherCAT segment, maintenance connections, and master privileges, and update in accordance with equipment shutdown procedures and a validation plan.
strings.5b62b00df38d14d26bf58dcecf9726aac2271d75: WooCommerce payment integrations: payment notifications and order status
strings.ecef00a953aa62b6163133f7cfb28da4fe6287b5: 6 issues published on 10/23 have been supplemented to reflect their inclusion in NVD. They affect individual plugins for CCAvenue, nexi Alpha Bank, Eurobank, iKhokha, OPay, and Mintpay, involving changes to states such as paid or canceled due to notification authenticity issues or a secret that is empty by default. They do not represent compromises of the banks themselves or WooCommerce itself.
strings.9e2256e0c6436f9f1dd288effe8f16f836f0fd6b: For iKhokha, check for version 3.0.4 or later. The original sources list no known fixed versions for the other 5, so consider suspending or replacing affected integrations and reconciling payments against payment provider records.
strings.26a8c56d6f3f235b5bb370df45649e3c1b199839: Pleasanter: rechecking the previously reported LDAP authentication issue
strings.64cacff6faa209f00747f86bf90dbbc8b7c3ce64: Following NVD inclusion of CVE-2026-113438, the developer's explanation from 10/23 was reviewed again. The affected conditions combine LDAP authentication on Linux/Docker or with the Windows Novell provider with AD or an LDAP server permitting anonymous binds. This is not an authentication bypass for all users, including those using local authentication, SAML, or passkeys.
strings.13a9497523ccfb97474687d39e606423a2bc9a29: For affected configurations, update to 1.5.9.1 or later. Note that 1.5.9.0 does not include the fix and that LDAP users are affected when LDAP+Local is used.
strings.1a4c2fe345a7a385eb811e49585eca6032bac883: V-SFT: NVD inclusion of 7 previously reported issues
strings.2c4e1283d1cb6575aaefc30c00db397bda5658fc: CVE-2026-107894–107900 are 7 issues previously listed using JVN information. Their inclusion in NVD this time does not mean 7 new incidents or 7 newly confirmed cases of exploitation. The requirement to open a crafted V7-format file on a design workstation still applies.
strings.96815335e7e13a0906f84b19cb130673c2edd910: Check use of 6.2.11.0 and earlier and handling of external design files, and review improvement information and patches for 6.2.12.0.
strings.4f25ead4d3633294e66925f57de1286798b63bd1: PHP2Shell: primary research observing execution in a limited honeypot setup
strings.d4ff28ee11e4aa91e3ff8d33ab046e2ef5aa6222: The researcher correlated HTTP requests with 35 Apache-child shell executions across 3 targets using PHP8.4.26, single-worker Apache mod_php, and 128MiB. Execution was under UID33; this does not mean 35 victims or root access. This article has not independently reanalyzed all PCAPs or run the PoC. The withdrawal of the connection to the government agency intrusion reported by Unit42 remains separately in effect.
strings.46b2d9f5ae77bf3ad407ee93446e22bf77c769dc: In addition to updating, investigate suspicious child processes, communications, and file creation originating from PHP workers, together with surrounding HTTP records. Do not use 500 errors or large cookies alone to determine successful exploitation or absence of harm.
strings.49f38a33b9ae47b483e91a621f2262e7a7c5acca: Tailworm: distinguish source fixes from distributed releases and stop unnecessary forwarding
strings.c69e54c75576b703a3bfc89726757f1b11ead9d0: Official PR21942 changes Unix forwarding to use authenticated local user credentials. Serve PR21931 has also been merged, but the latest stable versions are 1.104.2 and headscale0.29.6, and the earliest fixed version covering all of Tailworm remains undetermined in this review. Connection policy PR21944 is open. A merge into main does not establish that a fix has been distributed.
strings.f596992043e6f7dc9b26db3cd19e8333ed34e252: After confirming an alternative management path, review the temporary measure of setting TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 in the tailscaled service environment and restarting it to stop unnecessary forwarding. Do not treat check mode or this flag alone as completing fixes for every research finding.
strings.e5234f6a704b3a39dad51778e7f368fcc0ef7958: Microsoft 365: check MFA and registered devices as well as sessions
strings.1b901424fa9afe70a9b104b13604d6c3baf70648: Huntress reports 497 successful sign-ins across 79 organizations, at least 48 unauthorized Entra device registrations, MFA replacement, and inbox rules. Distinguish reuse of stolen sessions from subsequent persistence. The source does not establish 79 intrusions today or the same cause as ConnectWise.
strings.206b3faece7ed4a564e365bd23bd059f045d3901: Alongside session revocation and password changes, investigate registered devices, MFA methods, inbox rules, new enterprise applications, and consent grants, and remove unauthorized entries. Do not prioritize response solely by the number of failed attempts.
strings.c3029d775ed4ae7ba90101459377725c62f68580: Gheist: exfiltration of secrets through GitHub logs
strings.3d257e2ebde97815ef1a11ceb8fc4ca78fc3ea29: Wiz reports more than 850 accounts and over 13,500 suspicious branches involving stolen tokens. Workflows print secrets to logs, which are retrieved through the GitHub API before the runs are deleted. The public runs examined were blocked by approval holds, while execution and subsequent activity were observed in private / Enterprise environments. Branch counts are not counts of affected organizations.
strings.5b45523c0068351a5f084ddde7130a0d640716ad: Check for ci-sync- branches, sync-check workflows, runs deleted shortly after creation, and cloud-side role assumption. In repositories where execution occurred, revoke and replace tokens and accessible secrets, and investigate self-hosted runners and permissions. Do not approve pending suspicious workflows.
strings.e2b8cd556b9a4c5f7d98dc926c57019d21b602a8: uCreator: research into surveillance capabilities through modified APKs and containers
strings.bfcf851c0f4db9d234282f6c43717969000d43c7: The research analyzes modified APKs for Telegram, WeChat, and other apps, and hooks inside Onion Box containers. It demonstrates capabilities to obtain 2FA information, sessions, and similar data, but a reliable victim count remains undetermined. It does not prove that the entire chain worked on Android17 or that OS updates alone can prevent every case.
strings.9f0efd36df4ede7b8e5a35d4a543413cb89b6c49: Check distribution sources, signatures, and app provenance. If suspicious modified versions are present, investigate sessions and authentication methods from a safe device. Do not confirm infection solely from residual LSPatch files or add the previous year's infection counts to this case.
strings.34ae6f4c94bf51c3ee07b155332ce173b1bad6fd: Neat: confirm deployment completion separately for devices and the cloud
strings.7b3ee63018cfd71327bd050fe23020f620a413f9: This update removes the advisory's old statement that firmware was being prepared. strings.7cf0ee69cae2ac2945393e7789cef667b68ebfe3: KEV: Linux privilege escalation and missing ESX logging added
strings.a7f48c64e77bf7ef0271953f6c6fed4152a831fe: KEV version 2026.10.28 contains 1,762 entries. CVE-2026-46300 describes chaining with the 2 PHP flaws; forensicTriage is Yes and the deadline is 10/31. CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.
strings.97a474d143541095776a892ef4185d0b19aa1891: Check kernel and embedded-product updates, including the running version after restart. Use the ESX vendor response matrix and treat missing logs as an investigation limitation.
strings.27d419779db6ec12d36b1695a9dc0a42af50fb4e: From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty
strings.b3cdbfd2c74daf1c63227588c5981beea31246dc: Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.
strings.5375a67522f54afb02a4a419d2afb5e1f98e5a4d: Restrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.
strings.107bd01eec3874ca6523c04fb621c4c3f00f2b64: So-net: member information and some email passwords exposed
strings.d8556062fd9d6a6c1ca35a20bebd4d27a6efc965: The official 10/27 notice says access on 10/19 was detected on 23 and disclosure established on 24. It separately reports 2,141,986 So-net member records and 443,495 plala (S course) member records. Passwords for member records are distinct from email passwords in some mail services: the latter were exposed and reset on 27. The notice also reports 16 bank-account records and 7 notification records. Do not add these as a count of people.
strings.8060aa14341bb61b972b30112b272efd7858783d: Reset affected email passwords using the official guidance and change reused passwords elsewhere. Do not infer exposure in other services such as NURO.
strings.12d035792407707656fdaf6a8c9f055e3295fd3a: UNM Health: clinical and academic recovery, with a warning about follow-on scams
strings.ce3b85106c3b2cf9760c76817954cc16a5618b90: The official 10/28 update reports fully functional clinical operations and resumed classes and research. Ambulance diversion and interrupted outpatient surgery and appointments on 10/26 remain recorded as real impacts. The institution says some end-user devices were affected without penetration of core systems or servers. Attacker claims of stolen data or payment offers are not confirmed disclosure or compensation.
strings.c926ad551b752518c20c72ee053eeda4115c9087: Use official hospital channels to check rescheduled appointments. Do not engage with purported attackers or compensation offers.
strings.afb189e222c8b479bc8da0e568a4784b7f680474: Silent Train: long-term monitoring of infrastructure serving communications, government and transport
strings.9560c5679095091f2d9ae1462bcd12977c36260a: Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes ephemeral relay chains tracked since 2023 and operations targeting management infrastructure. Victim notifications cover multiple years, rather than incidents newly occurring in this review. The report lists communications, government, defense, universities, water, energy and transport among targeted sectors without providing individual outage durations or financial losses.
strings.c1cb80871587043e7f85a2945d21abec130e2453: Review exposed management interfaces, devices usable as relays and management-network telemetry. Do not rely solely on IP reputation.
strings.ae7e9544cd170a5618a5402f2a304ab5924736d6: Yamaha NWR100: unauthenticated command execution and CONFIG access
strings.89c283876c9c525b8faa1613150afcf98aab1833: CVE-2026-97854 allows unauthenticated OS command execution, scored 9.8 in CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 in v4.0. CVE-2026-109822 concerns unauthenticated access to generated CONFIG files. Rev.26.00.07 and earlier are affected; Rev.26.00.08 is fixed. Potential impact is not a count of actual compromises.
strings.ba20c6b5f369f1939bb003b20b22edac50e6425a: Update firmware. If delayed, restrict devices and source IP addresses allowed to access the Web GUI.
strings.4dee0782934aba535fcc695c49cfa19612b289f5: Yamaha Windows products: separate installer and service-path fixes
strings.1a62068b2cd4551c179d2d4051bb4e5bc790f2d8: LAN Monitor installers through Ver.1.9.3 have a DLL-loading issue, fixed in Ver.1.10.1; already installed software itself is unaffected by this installer issue. YMS-VPN8 / YMS-VPN8-CP through Ver.1.04.00 have unquoted service paths, fixed in Ver.1.07.00. The latter requires permission to write to the system drive.
strings.9ede901865ade890a0e2f588032a6e9d9d63fa8d: Use the official fixed releases and avoid running installers beside untrusted DLLs. Review shared Windows access and write permissions.
strings.47b59073d7d28a9063b0a37f4b80944832c93cea: Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update
strings.c56deb4738c52d0247c3e19bc141d98eb32605ae: In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. JVN advises updating to 7.4.0 or later and using struts.rest.anySetter.requireAnnotations=true with @StrutsParameter(allowDynamicKeys = true). Conditions include REST use and any-setter declarations; this does not establish compromise of all Struts applications.
strings.90ed777950b9eed4cad4f59e00dae90b60bcf227: Check the update, configuration and annotations together. Work around the issue by avoiding any-setter or validating values in the application before storage.
strings.363e509a0a994f5e01eee338ae0a6563e2855710: EDK II: distinguish PXE exposure from shipped firmware fixes
strings.da1cb60e8e5edaedef699b848330a6bada8c8c70: The official CVE-2026-97631 advisory describes pre-OS memory corruption by an attacker able to deliver ICMP errors during PXE boot. It identifies master as of 2026-09-14 and still lists Not patched currently. A fix PR does not prove a manufacturer has shipped a corrected BIOS or UEFI release.
strings.0185ceb99ee22b6c35ff0b95cfc0ae683b6f8f78: Disable unnecessary network boot and restrict PXE paths. Check firmware releases and deployment with the hardware supplier.

strings.8536a9cabf9cb3428c637f98e117f93f2912915e: Collection: NVD publication and last-modification queries are collected separately over fixed UTC windows, with pagination. strings.d493d2f009cf4599d0af1b4bb8c8af459af85c87: Cross-referencing and classification: CVE and GHSA IDs, reference URLs, vendor advisories, releases and public code are compared, retaining differences in affected conditions and fix status. strings.2487670777d6c322de66c2e3281c44157fc5bbfa: Timestamps and integrity: Disclosure, database registration, revision, retrieval, fix availability and restoration are kept distinct. strings.fd45a5f575abe8e71cd5029b01e775093188a049: Limitations: Responses are retrieval-time revisions collected after cutoff; recollection may not recover historical bodies. strings.03be2697827384a829ca3663616a1df09f8cbbec: Malicious packages: check each advisory published in this window
strings.7754a0a8cb08cccc6cc3640e982fc415e2fec37d: Malware advisories published in this window are retained by package. Similar names do not establish infection or a shared campaign, and an absent fixed version does not establish a safe release.
strings.66b24043f68807623908870c3f44a6fd4343aa13: Kubeflow Pipelines fixes archive expansion and log authorization
strings.60be1f914e46d55e6000af9ed9dabdf859909854: Archive uploads are decompressed before namespace authorization and can consume server memory when reachable. Separately, callers knowing a run ID and suitable node information can retrieve logs with API-server permissions. External authentication and network controls affect reachability.
strings.9600074a477ccebca7e3d19201fbc7651fec9271: Upgrade the product to 2.18.0 and review readLog permissions in custom roles. The narrative identifies releases through 2.17.3; the API lists commit-based Go pseudo-versions, which are not product release numbers.
strings.57801c4f27d00d95eb69a3410825ff3876d6c141: pypdf fixes loops and resource consumption in crafted PDFs
strings.ba14480021fff8b26e09503a68b1e61b0efde276: Incomplete xref data, dictionary cloning and page trees with shared resources can trigger loops or memory consumption. Other paths affect page labels, invalid dictionaries in strict mode, encrypted PDFs with incorrect Count values and cross-reference streams.
strings.a7c2ace41f08464fe66637182c7bea875b8baf68: Upgrade to 6.21.4 or later to cover all seven advisories; also bound processing time and memory for untrusted PDFs.
strings.dad2488795a803ed3d51287f4dceff6ebd9c1755: Joi multiple-email validation can exhaust CPU
strings.c40e9319c325519bdb131bd09e2871bf28457fda: Long whitespace runs cause quadratic splitting in string().email({ multiple: true }), blocking the event loop in applications validating untrusted input with this option.
strings.e64910c4642008c5bcd3b128238e30539e6228e7: Upgrade to a patched release. As a workaround put max before email and avoid abortEarly: false. Consider migrating from legacy @hapi/joi, for which the API lists no patched release.
strings.ec9dcf3201149e9c85e64d3182aa9f3916d39519: @hapi/content multipart header parsing can cause DoS
strings.d262ac8dcddc82e4f3160b943b674d27c38b47a7: Long malformed Content-Disposition parameters cause quadratic regex processing. Multipart-enabled hapi routes reach this parser before handlers and input validation.
strings.f23a024a2d1f6a2ad2a93974ce6f40ffe6122ef8: Upgrade to @hapi/content 6.0.3 or later and review legacy content dependencies. Lowering payload.maxBytes only reduces the impact.
strings.d557c336ffdb33c6e8a43de7778be04314eb5f9e: minimatch pattern optimization can amplify resource use
strings.5e1f815f3ac93e576bd3c9a27fe1dca6da149b6a: With optimizationLevel at least 2, attacker-controlled glob patterns can expand preprocessing entries and trigger costly subsequent comparisons, consuming CPU and memory.
strings.ebb46e62e31dab61f0ce44bb785e11413625c2fa: Upgrade to 11.0.1 or later and review untrusted-pattern inputs and optimization settings.
strings.19c6d185b0d660426ab426e03bb4f202bc51339a: Directory traversal can continue after AbortSignal cancellation or timeout. Services using cancellation as a budget for untrusted patterns or trees can accumulate background work.
strings.1a368d518d798229c92d7086b045b8f4078f4e75: Upgrade to 14.0.2 or later and review assumptions that timeouts stop traversal costs.
strings.ee13994e53fe34134de6275d654b6fe2fa0bf61e: Authlib client-management examples omit authorization binding
strings.7c7cc8c10059293b489507f4c25bb14252ef3166: RFC 7592 examples omit binding the registration access token to the target client. Providers following those examples can permit another valid client token to read, change or delete registrations; exposure depends on application implementations.
strings.dd9b9619472213328ab947b21f3d81e7a1020590: Consult corrected examples in 1.9.1 or later and bind token ownership to the target client_id in custom authenticate_client and check_permission methods.
strings.334e6716fb7d7537149d9bf2508c01d962bf2a75: pyasn1 fixes quadratic ASN.1 decoding paths
strings.82372e23edf613594c3851a85f953f59c4317c32: Attacker-controlled constructed BIT STRINGs and strings, binary REALs, indefinite-length ANY values and schemaless containers can consume disproportionate CPU. Exposure includes BER/CER and some DER paths, depending on type, schema and length form.
strings.2aa0eaf25a394ab7856261c3feeefaf1ed94f0e5: Upgrade to 0.6.5 or later. Earlier OID and REAL-conversion fixes do not cover these decoding paths.
strings.115fb8446ab81d92086b43a6c1a049e04e6dbf5e: node-forge fixes 11 crypto, certificate and TLS issues
strings.8f55e34c11ec3e9b8f8c0ead99009510eef7f41e: Issues include OID misencoding, prototype pollution in forge.http cookies, PEM/TLS denial of service and negative-input modInverse loops. Separate validation flaws affect zero-like AES-GCM tagLength, zero-iteration PKCS#12, CA stores with duplicate subjects and certificate chains using deprecated extension OIDs. Exposure depends on APIs and settings.
strings.5c70e67a8befe904730d1b50bdf9c8d231d76bd9: Upgrade to 1.4.1 or later. Review fixed valid GCM tag lengths, untrusted PEM/PFX inputs and forge TLS usage. The basicConstraints bypass requires a trusted CA to issue a certificate containing the crafted extension.
strings.a9c460d6187ea133c456703b43d2b3026e1799e3: PHPUnit shared temporary directory permits local code execution
strings.8563244232ac90a7a607ad897f735bb12ba664cb: During PHPT coverage runs in 13.4.0–13.4.3, another local user who creates the shared temporary directory first can replace test code and execute it as the test runner.
strings.c2f1788e5c7662d1ee58520d930d96b9bf7dbcf1: Upgrade to 13.4.4 or later; use a private per-user TMPDIR as an interim isolation measure.
strings.15be03a4f4cc4fa6eb0ead52210542a3dcf01fcb: Nuxt development servers expose secrets and readable files
strings.77405d35ac35c05dfac0e3a82b0f8e2f13dca01f: Network-reachable development servers can expose generated appSecret files and private config embedded in Nitro 2 development bundles. In 4.6.0–4.6.2, HMR client-error reports also allow reading files accessible to the dev process. Production builds are unaffected.
strings.0c346245a475beca01d3d1ff130498c582956ce7: Upgrade nuxt and @nuxt/vite-builder to 4.6.3 or later and restrict dev-port exposure. Rotate potentially exposed credentials and invalidate dev sessions as applicable. Nuxt 3 is end of life and requires migration.
strings.8889e9b1075e68517232cddda3bb7837e1b392e6: Nuxt dot segments bypass page-route path checks
strings.51563c525a1b05e10399adaf6f8a956e307247db: In 4.6.0–4.6.2, inconsistent normalization between page rendering and Nitro can bypass path-based server/middleware and route rules. API handlers and appMiddleware applied to resolved routes are unaffected.
strings.cd9bd3c8995363477fa8a5cd316822e75aa252c4: Upgrade nuxt and @nuxt/nitro-server to 4.6.3 or later; reject dot segments in an early middleware as a workaround.
strings.e1b55d9c24b9364c2eef94ed57045cf5cfa98a9b: @sigstore/oci sends registry credentials to cross-host upload locations
strings.2c1092dd978ccd4ada50b4d3561b3292ba3e0482: An unchecked blob-upload Location is used for a fresh PUT carrying the registry Authorization and custom authentication headers. This requires a malicious or compromised registry response. The report traces source code rather than an observed hostile-registry exchange.
strings.147128d2bc73e0182bf631818ee010a300a0c687: Upgrade to 0.7.2 or later and assess credential exposure if suspicious registries were used.
strings.f014e51f98a1ff81c874552b23d942a883a63c0c: MariaDB Connector/J hardens handling of hostile server replies
strings.e27958922c95b26e8af02c98ad7cd2de28513b87: Server-declared lengths, integer truncation and XA recovery data can trigger allocations or exceptions. With allowLocalInfile enabled, SQL matching flaws can disclose client files; undetected charset changes affect string integrity. All require control of server-side replies or a MitM position.
strings.4219a8cd56c53b20529e9002e97893d61437ea90: Upgrade to the applicable 3.3.7, 3.4.5 or 3.5.11 line covering all five issues. Disable allowLocalInfile when unnecessary and review trusted endpoints and TLS validation.
strings.2bf4fedbfc751525907daf5e5a786cba9e7d05c9: follow-redirects cross-realm arrays can expose custom credentials
strings.3645d19175e489d6b20e9268cd605098d8f15a00: In 1.16.0 and 1.16.1, cross-realm sensitiveHeaders arrays are discarded, allowing declared custom credentials to follow cross-origin redirects. Built-in Authorization and Cookie protections remain effective; the report does not establish Axios exposure.
strings.68af35bfc7bee990841632b02418b297eee65601: Upgrade to 1.16.2 or later and review wrappers and vm boundaries preserving custom-header options.
strings.c3397fd2284357f26498f51a68c3d8b5c7783f03: russh fixes missing signing confirmation and resource issues
strings.70d82ea8d9bce5bd15dc63822675192b3c46b1b0: Confirm-constrained agent keys can sign without calling Agent::confirm; agent-socket peers can also grow memory with repeated constraints. A hostile SSH peer can stall writes with a 0 maximum packet size, while repeated server EXT_INFO packets grow client memory.
strings.0a84c2e7e65b5c3648ac9221daf9ef52d240043f: Upgrade to 0.65.0 or later, check compatibility as custom confirm implementations are called again, and restrict agent forwarding.
strings.258e035ce0f855d7f595fe321623d25a55846bcc: pageant unchecked frame lengths permit memory consumption
strings.2d9986644446fa066b2091f4191fa6078514603e: PageantStream buffers peer-declared lengths without checking the transport’s 8 KiB limit. Oversized or incomplete frames consume retained memory when a peer controls stream bytes.
strings.8fe2ca89cf9988897a071c55509d7c8ccf2aeb70: Upgrade to 0.2.5 or later and review untrusted stream access through SSH agent forwarding or similar paths.
strings.4e975c6a829b4228a4656dd95c6b382d8bd83728: Repeated documents exceeding the validation-error limit extend a shared exception traceback, retaining documents and validation state. This affects the 3.3 line; GraphQL-core 3.2 and GraphQL.js are unaffected.
strings.767e9ae18adadc5bc10dcb68751d9382bf655a63: Upgrade to 3.3.1 or later. Execution-time depth or complexity limits alone do not address this validation-stage issue.
strings.951f516a6da73a19be096cd08aa874030c66cb94: OAuthLib token grants can authorize under a different client ID
strings.56a383d090cf0c5aff809f71be21eaa343143a4d: In client_credentials and password flows, a body-supplied client_id can differ from the authenticated client during authorization. Exposure requires valid lower-privilege client credentials and validators relying on the client_id argument for grants or scopes.
strings.75696d90f8645b579b081923ef1bc84f959dde1b: Upgrade to 4.0.0 or later and bind authorization to request.client, rejecting explicit ID mismatches before validation.
strings.17c8368d856a72f72a83fd03ad0763457b86d52f: OpenWISP Controller CRL API omits organization scoping
strings.b3e2929d511ac2b5d668db9376915627de428c31: Organization managers with CA-view permission can fetch another organization’s CRL by CA ID. Only issuer information and revoked serials are exposed, not private keys or modification capabilities. CRLs are public by default, making explicitly protected deployments more relevant.
strings.f21743351554acdf06875e3f618270e1d3cb5e96: Upgrade to 1.3.2 or later and verify organization scoping for CRL downloads.
strings.f2860ec08d05386099e65d88df1b7878ca09a21d: Fiber legacy CORS matching permits credentialed reads
strings.2c38343cb3e8e1c77cab7bfe7505582d7058ce48: In 2.52.1 and 2.52.2, wildcard matching omits dot-boundary and scheme checks, permitting unrelated domains with matching suffixes. Applications enabling AllowCredentials can expose authenticated responses cross-origin.
strings.d5ba05d1b9bbffca0af98b10c12ebcfec9c3da75: Upgrade to at least 2.52.3, preferably the latest v2. Separate matching hardening in 2.52.16 does not broaden this advisory’s affected range.
strings.71a1d52eba645793deff31ab4f132a8592c1f2ef: Signal K app-store icons permit SSRF
strings.8c714a027076382e2ba41d035f7ec791931b55e3: Absolute HTTP(S) icon URLs from listed plugins are fetched with redirects. An attacker able to list a plugin can induce server requests to internal addresses when the store is browsed. Testing exercised the real modules directly.
strings.99fa1849c7566fc52446ae51037021c3b6e5e99e: Upgrade signalk-server to 2.34.0 or later and review icon destinations and internal-network egress controls.
strings.47a27ad4e1d754611e8c1c5105cb90cee7d2ce40: Signal K traversal can lead to admin takeover and code execution
strings.bced71d1df110823fa476cbd6abb269548a41d18: Insufficient path validation in resources and applicationData APIs permits access outside storage roots. Reading the JWT secret in security.json enables forged admin tokens and execution through an Execute provider. Anonymous access requires readonly access enabled; default deployments require a readonly token.
strings.49034f65f7d40bcbfdd1c2de3017f07e058adca8: Upgrade signalk-server to 2.34.0 and @signalk/resources-provider to 1.5.3 or later. Assess exposure, rotate potentially exposed JWT secrets and credentials, and inspect persisted provider settings.
strings.19f22b9ccc06a8f79b4d4621872ccfb586cdf2f1: imgproxy ICO loading flaws corrupt heaps and allocate excessive memory
strings.5c4d53fbff7191143d23bdcb1f92c417a5cbdd28: Untrusted ICO sizes trigger integer overflow, out-of-bounds BMP-header reconstruction or unbounded allocation. Crafted images can crash workers; the overflow also carries potential code-execution risk, without demonstrating successful code execution.
strings.85d87c61e8a6344ceaef4b99669b74f1f540a6db: Upgrade to 4.0.17 or later to cover all three issues. Version 4.0.16 does not include the BMP-header reconstruction fix.
strings.8acd361eae2efbc126225ef9ccfb90909221672f: anacrolix/torrent deep bencode exhausts stack or CPU
strings.2100073fc681be807010712f936797ef107981d7: Unbounded bencode nesting in crafted torrent files or peer metadata can overflow the stack. Repeated subtree parsing in v2 file trees also causes quadratic CPU consumption.
strings.63351b35872d5e1751d1e4328fc0129d12ac20ef: Upgrade to a version containing commit 76452a2c8a2f; the Go API identifies 1.61.1-0.20260911233437-76452a2c8a2f as patched. Review nesting and processing budgets for untrusted metadata.
strings.863bb78c726bc4aabdc12815b7cafffda1b57980: AdminNeo fixes 7 SQLite, cookie, XSS, CSRF and cache issues
strings.cf9e68ccf2af055db593598e12c81716e381a82e: Issues include file creation or deletion by authenticated SQLite users, cookie-attribute injection through untrusted X-Forwarded-Prefix and XSS from hostile MySQL version strings. Observed CSRF tokens permit forgery, while version-cache poisoning causes persistent DoS. Code execution depends on additional conditions such as writing to a PHP-executable location.
strings.977aaa494ad762d0400929d349b45e78fb38f14b: Upgrade to 5.5.1 or later. Set trusted proxy prefixes and restrict database endpoints and PHP write permissions. Version 5.5.0 fixes the cache DoS alone; the other 6 require 5.5.1.
strings.34adb01e35e33f7583298e8a6bc73ee511922770: Emissary navigation URL validation fix is incomplete
strings.2a9e1627ee49da635797a7e2fa8e6e9e769a5292: The NavAction URL regex accepts protocol-relative and single-slash forms, reported to permit open redirects or SSRF. Actual exposure depends on input and fetching paths; successful internal credential theft is not established here.
strings.918ac43622359d0dddf7f4b10c25f963736c1921: Upgrade to 8.51.0 or later as identified by the API and review URI parsing and allowed-host validation. Distinguish commit identifiers in the prose from package versions.
strings.d13cded1686c50e45a32753b03e2b718019b3efe: pypi-publish updates trust store after CA revocation
strings.ceef3dc30d0e99d6ca338e89a7fd5f3300543d21: The notice removes the emSign root CA from the certifi trust store used by Sigstore for Trusted Publishing and Digital Attestations. The prose says before 1.14.2, but the structured API marks versions through 1.14.2 affected and 1.14.3 patched.
strings.5716ceb3910142f3b162e85ad3c23accbdb46c71: Use 1.14.3 or later to follow the conservative structured range and update pinned workflow references. Do not treat 1.14.2 as fixed based only on the prose.
strings.095f120eb441139ea619105dc4732dce86c6a3d8: joserfc JWS and JWE resource guards are insufficient
strings.09910dd782b4a2a5b900899b1207e3cc972767ae: Compact JWS copies segments before size checks, creating an additional input-sized allocation. General JSON JWE has no recipient-count bound and repeats RSA decryption per recipient; verify_all_recipients=False does not reduce that CPU work.
strings.4a2e5d0f76b0b05a0641bfe0ae41a095a15bbaff: Upgrade to 1.7.6 or later to cover both issues and bound token sizes and recipient counts at application boundaries.
strings.80a0cb926ad9be243c98069ae29676ad5d21f0ee: Soft Serve fixes stale private visibility and repository-name disclosure
strings.0380525803e28c0d0b076ce6fe446509f9baaf14: A race when making public repositories private can retain stale authorization and expose later commits. strings.e9bbc289b8a3080ff750bfde397ae876e748d739: Upgrade to 0.12.3 or later. Restarting clears stale visibility but does not prevent recurrence; create new repositories private from the outset as an interim measure.
strings.db91a3f35d7318df4e4646db3e5afb376b8d1593: Nx Maven and Gradle plugin options permit command injection
